adaptation: Standard layout adapted: the chart anchors on total money in (revenue $26.7M + non-cash warrant fair-value gain $127.2M = $153.9M) because the warrant gain is 4.8x revenue and a revenue-scaled chart cannot draw it. Net interest and other expense ($23.7M) is grouped with operating expenses, so the chart's operating line is the reported pre-tax income. Balance checks on the adapted model: total money in = left after direct costs + cost of revenue ($153.9M = $138.5M + $15.4M); left after direct costs = pre-tax income + operating expenses ($138.5M = $31.5M + $107.0M); pre-tax income - tax = net income ($31.5M + $0.1M tax benefit = $31.6M). Reported figures are unchanged: revenue $26.7M, operating loss -$71.9M, pre-tax income $31.5M, net income $31.6M.
verdict: Cipher's revenue fell 63% to $27M as Bitcoin mining wound down and its first HPC lease dollars arrived — and a $127M non-cash warrant gain, not operations, is what put the quarter in profit.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: Down 63% YoY — mining revenue fell as the HPC transition began

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: Basic EPS was +$0.08; diluted strips out the $127M warrant gain

kpis.label: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.note: vs +$41M a year ago — the company's own operating measure

kpis.label: Barber Lake contracted revenue
kpis.note: Lease expanded to a 20-year term in the quarter

segments.name: Bitcoin mining revenue
segments.note: Mining Bitcoin for its own account — still the biggest revenue line, but down 71% YoY as Cipher pivots to data centers.

segments.name: HPC leasing revenue
segments.note: Rent from high-performance computing data centers — the first HPC lease revenue Cipher has ever reported, from the Black Pearl site.

segments.name: Warrant fair-value gain
segments.note: A paper gain: Cipher's warrant liability shrank in value as its share price moved, so accounting rules book a gain. No cash arrived, and it reverses if the share price rises. Shown as a source because it is what turned the quarter profitable.

opex.name: Compensation & benefits
opex.note: Paying the team — it includes a large share-based pay bill as the company builds out its data center platform.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal and admin. Up sharply YoY as the platform scaled.

opex.name: Interest & other expense, net
opex.note: Interest expense of $59.0M on Cipher's growing data-center debt, less $32.7M of interest income on its cash pile and $2.6M of other income. Cipher reports this below its operating result; in this adapted layout it is grouped with operating expenses so the operating line equals reported pre-tax income.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of sites and equipment over their lives — much lower than a year ago as mining rigs were sold or sidelined.

opex.name: Power agreement & other operating losses
opex.note: A $13.9M paper loss from revaluing a power purchase agreement (the contract's market value moved against Cipher), plus $2.7M of other operating losses.

opex.name: Bitcoin fair-value & sale gains
opex.note: A $12.4M unrealized (paper) gain on the Bitcoin Cipher holds, as its price rose, plus a $0.5M realized gain on Bitcoin sold — together they reduced operating costs on paper.

opex.name: Power sales
opex.note: Selling power back to the grid — it reduced operating costs.

otherDetail: Interest and other items are grouped with operating expenses in this adapted layout (see the Interest & other expense line) — net interest and other expense was $23.7M, and the $127.2M warrant gain is shown as a source at the left of the chart.
follow100Note: Adapted for Cipher: this table is per $100 of total money in (revenue + the warrant gain), not per $100 of revenue — per $100 of revenue alone, the warrant gain would be about $476 and the table would be meaningless. On revenue alone, Cipher kept $118 of profit per $100 of revenue only because of that paper gain; operations lost money.
footerNote: Adapted layout — see one-time items. Figures in $M to three decimals so the lines add up exactly. Reported operating result was a $72M loss.

takeaways.title: A business in transition
takeaways.text: Revenue fell 63% to $26.7M: Bitcoin mining dropped 71% to $20.8M, partly offset by the first-ever HPC lease revenue of $5.9M from Black Pearl. The future is contracted, not current: the Barber Lake lease was expanded to 20 years, taking its contracted revenue to about $9.1B.

takeaways.title: Operations lost money
takeaways.text: The reported operating loss was $71.9M. Running costs included $38.6M of compensation, $26.4M of G&A and an $13.9M paper loss on a power agreement, partly offset by a $12.4M paper gain on Bitcoin held. Adjusted EBITDA — the company's own measure — was -$10M.

takeaways.title: A paper gain made the profit
takeaways.text: Net income was $31.6M only because of a $127.2M non-cash gain as Cipher's warrant liability fell in value. That is also why diluted EPS is -$0.22 while basic EPS is +$0.08: the diluted calculation strips the warrant gain back out.

oneTimers: Change in fair value of warrant liability: +$127.2M — a non-cash paper gain (the warrants Cipher owes became cheaper to settle as the share price moved). It is shown as a source in the chart, with the layout adapted and documented, because it is 4.8x revenue.

Bitcoin on the balance sheet was marked up by $12.4M (unrealized) in the quarter, and a power purchase agreement was marked down by $13.9M — both non-cash, both inside operating results as Cipher reports them.
Interest expense jumped to $59.0M from $1.3M a year ago as Cipher borrowed heavily to build data centers; interest income was $32.7M on its cash pile.
